correctness.rationale: Every maximal \(Q_d\) geodesic has length \(d\), so elementary vertex-volume counts give upper bounds \(3,5,9\) and cover lower bound \(10\). For \(Q_4\), all \(192\) unoriented diameter paths are exhaustively generated in two independent representations; by bit-translation and coordinate symmetry, the canonical path has \(31\) disjoint partners, and every two such partners intersect, excluding three-path packings. A direct third check excludes all triples and counts \(2976\) disjoint pairs. Explicit sequences for \(Q_5\) and \(Q_6\) give five and nine disjoint maximal geodesics, respectively; the nine \(Q_6\) paths miss only vertex \(47\), and a tenth path through that vertex covers the entire cube. The supplied verify.py reconstructs all finite conditions and generated output VERIFY_OK. Exhaustive finite enumeration is valid for the finite Q4 statement; no infinite extrapolation is asserted.

value.rationale: Hypercubes are canonical Cartesian powers, and the exact attainment of the geodesic-volume bound is a natural gap in the 2022 foundational packing result. The \(Q_4\) failure of sharpness alongside \(Q_5,Q_6\) attainment gives a genuinely structural boundary, while the exact \(Q_4\) packing enumerator and reproducible obstruction exceed a routine application of the bound. The \(Q_6\) ten-path cover closes the 2026 explicit published interval 10..16 in the first dimension beyond the small cases whose exact coverings the source considered. All results are self-contained, natural finite cases, not unsupported general asymptotic claims.
